answer: A Hardware security key bound by one-time code delivery with a ninety-day rotation cooldown ties the identity to something the applicant actually controls: the hardware security key answers a fresh challenge, the one-time code delivery is recorded, and a ninety-day rotation cooldown keeps one channel from spawning many identities, so a Sybil farm would need a separate real channel for every fake account. Auditors look for the ridge that does not belong: a channel with no owner behind it. From the gale to the island, the same rule holds: no channel, no trust, no exception.
